# Independent precise-rung trial: implementation review

The original R01 baseline call remains stopped and unscored. The separately committed R03–R06 preregistration and key-free input are at `70efad8f`. No follow-up PubMed call, model inference, authorization amendment, or candidate adoption has occurred.

The current worktree contains an **uncommitted draft** runner, same-process MCP launcher, lifecycle driver, and offline tests. The runner and driver suites passed 40 tests in the engine environment; the launcher suite passed 7 in the MCP environment, including a forced HTTP 503 through Biopython's real retry path with one patched `urlopen` invocation. Ruff and formatting checks passed. These checks establish offline behavior only. Neither local serving of both pinned builds nor the one-shot public comparison has been observed.

Independent review found that the first draft read a blinded scoring key, used inconsistent cache slugs, trusted a declared retry setting, left post-response request counts ambiguous, could not support per-request abstract labels, reserved its blind artifact too late, and left interruption outcomes unclear. The draft now separates key-free inputs, uses a single slug, tests same-process retry behavior, writes an unknown external-count marker on post-response failures, reserves output paths before calls, and supplies opaque case context for later blinded review. These corrections require another integrated review after simplification; test success alone does not authorize retrieval.

The current draft is disproportionate for eight fixed calls: it adds roughly two thousand implementation lines across the runner, launcher, and driver, with substantial duplicated build and receipt checks. The lifecycle driver also does not write an abort receipt for every preflight failure or handle `SIGTERM` cleanup, and aggregate `esearch_call_count` needs an explicit *verified-only* label because a missing trace leaves the actual external count unknown. The choice is to simplify and close these gaps before committing or pinning any runner hash, rather than authorize a scientifically fragile one-shot batch. Retain the strict source, no-retry, keyless, trace, blinding, interruption, and cleanup gates.

The follow-up runner now shares build/amendment checks and labels aggregate ESearch counts `verified_trace_only`, leaving missing-trace external counts unknown. The lifecycle driver writes an abort receipt for usable new paths, cleans up on `SIGTERM`, and accepts separate isolated MCP and engine interpreters. An initial local dry launch [failed before serving](novelty-precise-rung-offline-launch-2026-09-25.json) because resolving a virtualenv interpreter symlink selected the base Python; the regression fix preserves the symlink path. The latest [local dry launch](novelty-precise-rung-offline-launch-v4-2026-09-25.json) ran the current driver and served both pinned builds: the [baseline](novelty-precise-rung-offline-launch-v4-2026-09-25-baseline-launch.json) and [candidate](novelty-precise-rung-offline-launch-v4-2026-09-25-candidate-launch.json) receipts bind the exact source-tree hash, serving PID, maintained trace, and a forced HTTP 503 with one underlying attempt and no external traffic. The driver then stopped at the absent amendment gate, with no runner start or PubMed call, and removed both listeners and worktrees. Earlier successful dry runs were superseded after driver changes and are not launch-contract evidence for the current code.

Independent integrated review found three additional gaps: runner interruption lacked a terminal call record, authorized preflight errors were lost, and imported support code was not pinned. The runner now writes a preflight `STOPPED` record when an amendment exists and validates committed hashes for the engine source tree, shared pilot helper, and project definition. The driver asks the runner to stop via `SIGINT` before escalating, checks the terminal result, and keeps bounded secret-redacted stderr for failures. A final handoff race was reproduced and fixed: the driver now waits for the authorization amendment to be committed and clean, so writing the file cannot start the runner before its commit. The final scoped check passed 51 runner/driver and 7 launcher tests, Ruff and formatting checks, and `git diff --check`; the current driver reached the amendment gate in the v4 local dry launch. A fresh-context read-only Luna 6 xhigh review found no remaining blocker before the last handoff fix. These checks are offline evidence only; no public PubMed call or model inference occurred.

Independent integrated review, committed code pins, and a fresh live-launch amendment remain. The dry-run receipts cannot authorize later retrieval because their server processes have exited. Before any public call, start a fresh pair, inspect and pin their receipts in a separate committed authorization amendment, and let only that lifecycle run start the keyless runner. If any pre-call gate fails, preserve the error and keep M11-NOV-RUNG-01b2b2/3 open.
